2026_014_fy27_budget_book_combined_file_.paragraph: Oakland Schools' proposed original budget for fiscal year 2026-27, dated 03/24/2026, covers the intermediate school district's General Education, Special Education and Career Focused Education funds plus its special revenue, debt service, capital projects, enterprise and internal service funds, with five-year forecasts and a five-year capital outlay plan attached. Proposed total funding is $563.2 million and proposed total expenditures are $591.7 million. The largest single line is the Public Act 18 special education base distribution to local districts, budgeted at $189,106,200, an increase of approximately $5.2 million or 2.9%, underwritten by property tax revenue budgeted to grow 3.4%.

**Document.** Oakland Schools proposed "Original Budget for the fiscal year 2026-27," printed 03/24/2026 and carried in the Troy Board of Education's May 19, 2026 materials. Oakland Schools is one of 56 Michigan intermediate school districts established in 1962. Budgets take effect July 1, 2026; the ISD board must submit its proposed budget to each constituent district board for review and comment not later than May 1, with adoption no later than June 30 following a public hearing.

**Enterprise-wide funding - $563.2 million**

| Source | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Property taxes | $270.7 million |
| Other local and investment revenue | $51.7 million |
| State source revenue | $24.8 million |
| Other financing sources and indirect revenue | $15.8 million |
| Estimated grant award funding | $200.2 million |

**Enterprise-wide expenditures - $591.7 million**

| Category | Amount |
| --- | --- |
| Salary, wage, and benefits | $88.8 million |
| Purchased services, supplies, utilities and dues/fees | $27.2 million |
| Capital outlay | $23.9 million |
| Transfers to LEAs and other funds | $233.4 million |
| Grant related expenditures | $200.2 million |
| Payment on existing debt | $18.2 million |

Both totals are net of eligible inter-company eliminated Risk Related Activity Fund amounts.

**Three major operating funds, FY 2026-27 proposed**

| Fund | Revenue | Expenditures | Ending fund balance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| General Education (100) | $28,635,100 | $27,413,900 | $16,655,400 |
| Special Education (200) | $216,559,900 | $221,496,800 | $17,212,700 |
| Career Focused Education (600) | $57,922,100 | $57,539,400 | $8,372,300 |

**Property taxes.** Budgeted to rise 3.4%, a conservative figure against Oakland County Equalization's expectation of just over 4.0% growth in county taxable values. By fund: General Education $15,547,600 to $16,076,200; Special Education $197,835,800 to $204,562,200; Career Focused Education $48,379,700 to $50,024,600; total $261,763,100 to $270,663,000, a change of $8,899,900. The tax base is 70% principal residence and 30% non-principal residence, and the District experienced a Headlee rollback in ten of the last eleven years. The Michigan Tax Tribunal reserve is set at .25% of tax revenues, approximately $676,700.

**PA-18.** The base distribution to local districts is budgeted at $189,106,200, with an additional $2,450,000 for group home and medical student support, incarcerated youth, startup assistance, extraordinary contingency, assistive technology and Section 24 payments. A supplemental PA-18 distribution of $5.8 million went to LEAs in December 2025 after the FY 2025 audited fund balance exceeded the 5% target.

**Staffing and compensation.** A net 7.2 FTE increase takes staffing from 642.9 to 650.1: minus 1.0 FTE Human Resources Manager, minus .5 FTE Business Office Residency Program, minus .3 FTE District & School Services part-time, plus 1.0 FTE Warehouse Supervisor, plus 6.0 FTE for a new Special Populations Continuum of Supports unit, plus 2.0 FTE for Artificial Intelligence. An across-the-board 2.0% pay increase is budgeted; the collective bargaining agreement expires June 30, 2027. The blended MPSERS rate is 26.53%; the Basic/MIP with Premium Subsidy rate falls from 29.91% to 27.51% on October 1, 2026. Health care hard caps assume 4.0% medical CPI growth: family $21,660.30 to $22,526.71, individual plus one $16,609.38 to $17,273.76, single $7,942.09 to $8,259.77.

**Debt and capital.** Principal redemption rises to $16,490,000 as the Qualified School Construction Bonds mature in May 2027 at $14.8 million; total debt service expenditures are $18,186,700. A partial refunding of the 2016 Refunding Bonds was underway at printing and will be handled in the first FY 2026-27 amendment. The five-year capital outlay plan totals $17,225,000 for 2026-27 and $92,037,800 across FY26-FY31.

**Identification and statutory context.** Oakland Schools' "Original Budget for the fiscal year 2026-27," a combined external budget book printed 03/24/2026, appearing in Troy School District Board of Education materials dated May 19, 2026. Oakland Schools is one of 56 Michigan intermediate school districts established in 1962, an autonomous tax-supported district under Michigan General School Law; its mission statement is "Every Student. Every Day." Cited compliance obligations are the General Property Tax Act (Public Act 206 of 1893, MCL 211.24e), the Uniform Budgeting and Accounting Act (Public Act 2 of 1968), and the Revised School Code (Public Act 451 of 1976, MCL 380.624 and MCL 380.684). The ISD board must submit its proposed budget to each constituent district board for review and comment by May 1; adoption follows a public hearing and must occur by June 30 for the year beginning July 1, 2026. Governing policies are 3050 (budget preparation), 3100 (annual operating budget and amendments), 3150 (fund balance) and 3170 (budget transfer authority); amendments come at least three times a year, and Board Policy 3230 requires reporting of cooperative-service subsidies.

**Enterprise-wide totals.** Proposed total funding is $563.2 million: property taxes $270.7 million; other local and investment revenue $51.7 million; state source revenue $24.8 million; other financing sources and indirect revenue $15.8 million; estimated grant award funding $200.2 million. Proposed total expenditures are $591.7 million: salary, wage and benefits $88.8 million; purchased services, supplies, utilities and dues/fees $27.2 million; capital outlay $23.9 million; transfers to LEAs and other funds $233.4 million; grant-related expenditures $200.2 million; payment on existing debt $18.2 million. Both are net of eligible inter-company eliminated Risk Related Activity Fund amounts.

**Revenue assumptions.** Property tax revenue is budgeted up 3.4%, or $9.0 million, a conservative estimate against Oakland County Equalization's projection of just over 4.0% county taxable value growth; taxable values reached pre-recession levels in 2022-23. The tax base is 70% principal residence and 30% non-principal residence, and the District saw a Headlee rollback in ten of the last eleven years. By fund: General Education Fund $15,547,600 to $16,076,200; Special Education Fund $197,835,800 to $204,562,200; Career Focused Education Fund $48,379,700 to $50,024,600; total $261,763,100 to $270,663,000, a change of $8,899,900. The Michigan Tax Tribunal reserve is budgeted at .25% of tax revenues, approximately $676,700. Investment revenue totals $7,893,400 against $8,778,500, most funds down 20.0% while Debt Service Funds rise from $419,000 to $1,206,000. Other local revenue totals $43,764,200 against $42,095,900. State source revenue totals $24,811,800 against $25,599,000; Section 81 ISD Operations rises 2.0%, Section 27L(4) Healthcare Offset one-time funding is removed, and Section 147a(2) MPSERS Normal Cost Offset loses a one-time adjustment. Grant revenue totals $200,249,800 (state $136,389,300, federal $61,993,900, local $1,866,600).

**Personnel and benefits.** Staffing moves from 642.9 to 650.1 FTE, a net 7.2 increase: elimination of a 1.0 FTE Human Resources Manager; a .5 FTE reduction in the Business Office Residency Program, from four residents to three for part of the year; a .3 FTE reduction in District & School Services Pupil Services part-time staff; a new 1.0 FTE Shipping/Receiving Warehouse Supervisor; 6.0 FTE for the new Special Populations Continuum of Supports unit; and 2.0 FTE in Technology Services for Artificial Intelligence. An across-the-board 2.0% increase applies to all staff; the collective bargaining agreement expires June 30, 2027. Non-union step growth is assumed at 1.3% and union wage base growth at .9%. Salaries and wages with FICA total $58,380,000 against $56,006,500. Employers pay an additional $28.10 in retirement costs per $100 of wages; eight MPSERS rates are in effect, the Basic/MIP with Premium Subsidy rate dropping from 29.91% to 27.51% effective October 1, 2026 and the MPSERS UAAL Stabilization Rate from 15.02% to 13.51%; the blended budgeting rate is 26.53% and MPSERS costs total $21,049,200. Health care uses the hard cap with 4.0% medical CPI growth: family $21,660.30 to $22,526.71; individual plus one $16,609.38 to $17,273.76; single $7,942.09 to $8,259.77. Employees contribute roughly 17% on average. Healthcare insurance totals $6,926,500 and other benefits $2,429,300, with dental up 7.5% and life and disability up 2%; workers compensation runs through the SET-SEG Self-Insurers Workers' Compensation Fund pool. The FICA rate is 7.65%, its 6.2% social security component applied to wages up to $184,500 for calendar year 2026.

**General Education Fund (100).** Revenue of $28,635,100 and expenditures of $27,413,900 produce an operating surplus of $1,221,200. Revenue is property taxes $16.1 million (56% of total), other local $4.3 million, state $7.5 million and other financing sources $.7 million. Expenditures are General Administration $3,428,200, Finance & Operations $10,750,400, Instructional Programs & Services $10,923,100 and Plant & Fixed Charges $2,312,200. Department budgets include Technology Licensing $2,206,000, Artificial Intelligence $911,000, Application Services $2,233,900, Early Childhood $1,131,300 (staff reallocated from grants after the loss of Great Start Collaborative funding), Shipping & Receiving $188,200 and Capital Outlay $870,000; Operating Transfers Out drops to $638,400 after a one-time $1.0 million transfer to the Career Focused Education Fund in 2025-26. Ending fund balance is $16,655,400 - non-spendable prepaids $66,400, assigned $12,407,300 and unassigned $4,181,700, or 15% of budgeted expenditures. The five-year forecast assumes property tax growth of 2.7% in 2027-28 and 2.6% for 2028-29 through 2031-32, and carries safety/security placeholders of $4,500,000 and $4,400,000 plus $2,426,000 of CTE Programming in 2027-28; unassigned fund balance is forecast at $4.4 million (12.7%), $5.5 million (16.7%), $6.3 million (21.3%), $6.1 million (20.2%) and $5.5 million (17.5%). Fund 105 grant projects total $139,536,500.

**Special Education Fund (200).** Revenue of $216,559,900 (property taxes $204.6 million, or 94%; other local $2.5 million; state $9.2 million; other financing $0.3 million) against expenditures of $221,496,800, an operating deficit of $4,936,900. Expenditure groups are Program Supervision & Direction $2,923,200, Program Operations $13,183,900, Plant & Fixed Charges $8,681,400, PA-18 Distribution $189,106,200 and LEA Transfers & Program Subsidies $7,602,100. Ending fund balance is $17,212,700: $15,934,100 restricted for future center facility renovations, $1,239,400 restricted for special education (5% of expenditures net of LEA transfers) and $39,200 non-spendable. Oxford Community Schools was approved for $5.6 million across FY26 and FY27 to construct an Autism Spectrum Disorder Center Program, contingent on twenty-five years of special education use; the FY 2026-27 line is $5,009,100. The department serves approximately 22,800 students with an Individualized Education Program, and the new Continuum of Supports unit adds a Supervisor, Social Worker, ASD Consultant, School Psychologist, Board Certified Behavior Analyst and Speech and Language Pathologist. LEA base distributions are projected at $194,028,200 for 2027-28, then $198,582,100, $203,278,700, $208,171,400 and $213,183,800. Capital outlay stays flat at $378,500 annually. Fund 205 grant projects total $57,765,900.

**Career Focused Education Fund (600).** Revenue of $57,922,100 (property taxes $50.0 million, 86% of total) and expenditures of $57,539,400 leave a surplus of $382,700 and an ending fund balance of $8,372,300, restricted portion $8,329,300 (14%). Expenditures are Campus Operations $24,599,500, District & Campus Support Operations $4,954,100, LEA Transfers & Program Subsidies $6,264,000 and Plant & Fixed Charges $21,721,800. Campus totals are Northwest $5,761,400, Southeast $5,928,200, Northeast $6,722,700 and Southwest $6,187,200; the four Oakland Schools Technical Campuses serve roughly 2,600-2,700 students each semester from all 28 constituent districts. LEA subsidies include Transportation Support $1,800,000, Career Readiness Allocation $3,678,100, OCCRA $112,600, Camps $100,000, STEM $131,300 and NAIS $442,000. Oakland County Sheriff's Department school resource officers, one per campus, become 100% locally funded beginning August 1, 2026. Restricted fund balance is forecast at $9.4 million (16.1%), $10.2 million, $11.0 million, $12.1 million and $12.7 million (19.7%). Fund 605 grant projects total $2,947,400.

**Other funds.** Shared Services & Tuition Programs Fund 270: revenue $20,987,000, expenditures $21,267,700, committed ending balance $3,703,500; VLAC K-8 is projected at 250 FTE at $6,450 resident and $6,650 non-resident tuition, VLAC 9-12 at 300 FTE at $6,700 and $6,900, and the Accelerated College Experience at 300 students at $4,900, all unchanged from 2025-26; foreign exchange payments to LEAs rise from $4,000 to $5,000 per student with mini-grants up to $5,000, partnering with KCK, Inc. for about 30 students. Oakland Network for Education Fund 271 links twenty-nine consortium members: revenue $1,474,400, expenditures $1,831,100 including Literacy Essentials Oakland $301,700 and the Numeracy Initiative $300,000, committed balance $12,349,800. Medicaid Fund 273: revenue and expenditures both $18,916,300, with $15,000,000 in Medicaid fees, $1,800,000 outreach and $1,356,200 Caring 4 Students transferred to LEAs; the program is expected to generate about $18.2 million for LEAs. HR/Finance Consortium Fund 277 (MiPEER, twenty districts, BusinessPlus): revenue $1,369,200, expenditures $1,300,600, committed balance $961,300, after $4,875,000 was transferred from the CPDI Fund between FY 2012-13 and FY 2015-16. School Activities Fund 290 budgets $180,000 in and out with a $268,600 balance. Debt Service Fund 311 (2016 Refunding Bonds, schedule through 2036) pays $1,690,000 principal and $771,700 interest, ending at $11,164,100; Fund 313 transfers $473,600 and ends at zero; Fund 314 pays $14,800,000 principal and $925,000 interest on the term bond, takes a $762,700 federal interest subsidy, and ends at zero. Capital Projects Fund 404 shows interest of $592,000 plus an $8,800,000 CFEF transfer for $9,392,000 of revenue and $16,508,100 of expenditures - $1,800,000 in safety and security trade contracts, $3,810,000 for OSTC-Southeast rooftop unit replacements, $4,900,000 for NAIS building alterations, $1,000,000 for robotics, $200,000 for the STEMi - leaving $9,991,600; the accompanying narrative instead cites revenue of $10.2 million and expenditures of $21.8 million. Fund 406 (Administration Building, allocated 50% GEF / 24% SEF / 26% CFEF) has revenue of $832,000 and expenditures of $5,261,100, ending at $6,678,800. Production Printing Enterprise Fund 710 shows operating revenue of $907,300, expenses of $1,088,500 and total net position of ($964,500) after GASB 68 and GASB 75. Risk Related Activity Fund 810 ends at $3,186,200 on revenue of $10,806,100 and expenses of $10,701,500; compensated absence accruals total $3.7 million.

**Programs, subsidies and initiatives.** Cooperative-service subsidies total $1,417,700: Xello career cruising software $360,000, Illuminate DnA $376,000, Pathful (Nepris) $250,000, Atlas Rubicon $217,300, Discovery Education Streaming/Learn 360 $78,000, STAMP $60,000, Lightcast Alumni Pathways $45,000 and CDX Automotive $31,400. Oakland Schools provides up to $5 million for Literacy Essentials Oakland, aligned with PA 146, the K-12 Literacy and Dyslexia Law. A Director of AI Strategy and Innovation was hired in September 2025, with an AI Solutions Architect and AI Implementation Consultant added here; cybersecurity work protects approximately 700 servers. Training counts as of early 2026: 695 PREPaRE Workshop 1 participants from 21 of 28 districts and 427 in Workshop 2 from 27 of 28; 663 Behavioral Threat Assessment and Management participants from 23 districts plus 26 resource officers, ahead of legislative requirements effective October 1, 2026; and 313 suicide-prevention participants from 26 districts trained with Dr. Steven Brock. Early Childhood cites savings of $160,900 annually on recruitment marketing, $475,400 on care coordination in 2025-2026 and $47,700 on developmental screening. Cost allocation runs 50%/25%/25% across GEF/SEF/CFEF generally, 27%/25%/48% FTE-based, 50%/24%/26% by space utilization, 73%/25%/2% by transportation miles and 6%/75.5%/18.5% for property taxes, totaling $28,800,000 or 9.46%. Discrimination complaints route to the Assistant Superintendent of Human Resources at (248) 209-2429 or Civil Rights/Title IX Coordinator Laura Richards-Farwell at (248) 209-2590.
